cases.title: Contention Wall
cases.description: Rust drives 100 OS threads through one shared AtomicI64. Kain currently has no user-level OS-thread fanout in LLVM, so this is the zero-lock collapse proxy over the same total increment count.
cases.fairness_note: Do not read this as a completed concurrency win. It is the benchmark shape Kain must graduate toward once collapse can be shared safely across spawned workers.

cases.title: Ghost Mirror
cases.description: Rust mirrors a 1 MiB payload through a std TCP loopback channel. Kain mirrors authority state with entangle and mutates a 1 MiB helper-owned buffer in-process.
cases.fairness_note: Kain entangle is currently in-process world mirroring, not a two-process transport. This case measures serialization/transport tax versus compiler-owned mirror semantics.

cases.title: Evolutionary Loop
cases.description: Rust uses runtime feature detection to choose a math lane. Kain expresses the same decision as converge/orchestrate lanes.
cases.fairness_note: Current Kain converge records and selects lanes; it does not yet race AVX-512 kernels or autotune silicon. This benchmark is the durable harness slot for that future backend.

cases.title: Scoped Ownership Memory Cell
cases.description: A smaller first-class ownership smoke benchmark: Kain uses collapse/observe/decay over a helper-owned heap cell; Rust uses an owned Box mutation and drop.
cases.fairness_note: This is a direct memory-lifecycle smoke, not a contention test.
